questions.markdown:
Test for consistency and solve the following system of linear equations by Gauss elimination method.

$$
\begin{aligned}
2x_1 + x_2 + 2x_3 + x_4 &= 6 \\
6x_1 - 6x_2 + 6x_3 + 12x_4 &= 36 \\
4x_1 + 3x_2 + 3x_3 - 3x_4 &= -1 \\
2x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 + x_4 &= 10
\end{aligned}
$$

Find all the eigenvalues and the eigenvector corresponding to the smallest eigenvalue of the matrix.

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}
2 & -1 & 1 \\
0 & 1 & 6 \\
0 & 3 & 4
\end{pmatrix}
$$

Use Gauss Seidel method to solve the system of linear equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}
3x + y + z &= 9.3 \\
x - 2y + 10z &= 30.6 \\
2x + 5y - z &= 10.5
\end{aligned}
$$

Perform 3 iterations and correct the solution up to 4 decimals by taking the initial approximation as.

$$
x^{(0)} = 1, \quad y^{(0)} = 2, \quad z^{(0)} = 3.
$$

Apply Gram Schmidt orthogonalization process to construct an orthonormal basis of from the following linearly independent set

$$
S = \{a_1 = (-2,1,2),\; a_2 = (-7,2,1),\; a_3 = (-11,-11,-1)\}.
$$

questions.markdown:
Let $T: \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be a linear transformation such that

$$
T(x,y,z) = (x - 3y - 2z, y - 4z, z).
$$

Then prove that $T$ is an invertible linear operator on $\mathbb{R}^3$. Also find $T^{-1}(-7,\ 4,\ -1)$.

Use method of variation of parameter to solve

$$
(D^2 - 3D + 2)y = \sin(e^{-x})
$$

Trace the parametric curve

$$
x = 2(t + \sin t), \quad y = 2(1 + \cos t)
$$

with suitable justifications.

Diagonalize the matrix

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix}
1 & 4 \\
2 & 3
\end{pmatrix}
$$

and hence compute $A^5$.

Use Newton Raphson method to find the approximate real root of

$$
f(x) = \sin x - \frac{x+1}{x-1}
$$

with initial approximate root $x_0 = -0.4$. Carry out 4 iterations correct to 4 decimal places.

Use Modified Euler's method to find approximate value of $y(1.5)$, given that

$$
\frac{dy}{dx} = x^2 e^{(x-y)}
$$

with $y(1) = 0.2$. Take $h = 0.25$ and carryout 3 iterations in each step, correct to 4 decimal places.

Use Newton's divided difference formula to determine as a polynomial in for the following data.

| $f(x)$ | 168 | 147 | 120 | 72 | 63 |
